Each claim is decided by the rule for its category. Within a rule, every exception clause is only considered if the clause immediately before it applied; when an exception applies, its decision replaces the previous one.

Rule 1 (flood): flood items are denied by default. Exception: if the home was occupied at the time, it is covered instead. Further exception to the previous clause: if maintenance records were not provided, it is denied. However, in that case, if a monitored alarm was installed, it is covered. Further exception to the previous clause: if the claimed loss is over $20500, it is denied. Even then, if the policy tier is platinum, it is covered.
Rule 2 (electrical surge): electrical surge items are covered by default. Exception: if no police report was filed, it is denied instead. Further exception to the previous clause: if the damage was assessed by an agent, it is covered. Even then, if maintenance records were not provided, it is denied. But if, in addition, the policy tier is standard, it is covered after all. Further exception to the previous clause: if the home was vacant at the time, it is denied.

However, in that case, if no receipt is attached, it is rejected.

However, in that case, if it was pre-approved by a Manager, it is reimbursed. However, in that case, if it was not paid with the corporate card, it is rejected. Even then, if the vendor is on the preferred list, it is reimbursed.

But if, in addition, the borrower is a graduate student, it is approved after all. Further exception to the previous clause: if the loan is longer than 7 days, it is refused. Even then, if unpaid fines exceed $84, it is approved.

But if, in addition, the home is at most 31 years old, it is denied after all.
Rule 3 (electrical surge): electrical surge items are denied by default. Exception: if the incident was reported within 57 days of it happening, it is covered instead. Even then, if no police report was filed, it is denied. Even then, if the policy tier is premium, it is covered. Further exception to the previous clause: if there are at most 2 prior claims in the last 3 years, it is denied. Each loan is decided by the rule for its category. Within a rule, every exception clause is only considered if the clause immediately before it applied; when an exception applies, its decision replaces the previous one.

Rule 1 (microfilm): microfilm items are approved by default. Exception: if a digital copy is available, it is refused instead. But if, in addition, the borrower has overdue items, it is approved after all. Even then, if the item is older than 122 years, it is refused. Even then, if unpaid fines are at most $80, it is approved. Even then, if the request is not signed by no one, it is refused.
Rule 2 (rare manuscripts): rare manuscripts items are refused by default. Exception: if the borrower is a visiting scholar, it is approved instead. However, in that case, if the item is on a course reading list, it is refused. Further exception to the previous clause: if the loan is at most 32 days, it is approved. But if, in addition, it is requested outside the exam period, it is refused after all. However, in that case, if the borrower currently has more than 10 items on loan, it is approved.
Rule 3 (reference books): reference books items are approved by default. Exception: if the borrower has overdue items, it is refused instead. But if, in addition, the loan is longer than 24 days, it is approved after all. Further exception to the previous clause: if it is requested outside the exam period, it is refused. Even then, if no digital copy is available, it is approved. Even then, if unpaid fines are at most $43, it is refused.

CASE
- Loan 1 (category: microfilm) - digital copy available: yes; borrower: a faculty member; request signed by: no one; unpaid fines: $83; has overdue items: yes; requested loan length: 53 days; item age: 142 years.
- Loan 2 (category: reference books) - holding branch: the law library; requested during exam period: no; items currently on loan: 0; requested loan length: 25 days; digital copy available: no; has overdue items: yes; unpaid fines: $43.
